text:
rachel: quick sync before the canary ramp for release/2026. plan is minimal: route tweak + canary traffic shift. want explicit rollback criteria set before applying.

tom: agree. propose rollback if error-rate > 0.8% sustained for 5m or cpu > 85% on inference nodes for 3 consecutive samples. also fail if infra apply introduces any new IAM trust changes (we should split those out).

vishal: +1 to thresholds. also add a soft-failure: if tail latency p95 increases >20% over baseline for 10m, pause and evaluate.

rachel: noted. we'll document thresholds in the runbook and wire alerts. ops-oncall can you create the PagerDuty rule for the canary?

ops-oncall: creating PD rule now. will set a severity-1 if error-rate >0.8% for 5m and will page infra oncall. also adding a non-paging warning for the p95 latency >20%.

deploy-bot: preflight running: `terraform plan -var-file=release-2026-canary.tfvars -target=module.net.route_fix`

deploy-bot: preflight result: plan OK but provider constraint mismatch across modules detected (modules/net uses `>=4.2` while modules/iam pins `~>4.2.1`). recommendation: pin provider in workspace to prevent drift during canary.

tom: we shouldn't mix provider changes in this window. can someone stage a workspace override pin then rerun plan?

vishal: i'll push a tiny workspace override and re-run. command: `terraform init -upgrade=false` and added `provider \"aws\" { version = \"~>4.2.1\" }` in the workspace override.

deploy-bot: re-run preflight: plan OK. no IAM changes detected. network apply queued: `terraform apply -target=module.net.route_fix -auto-approve`

rachel: before apply, posting rollback snippets in thread so they're easy to copy:
- quick rollback to previous route state: `terraform apply -target=module.net.route_fix -var-file=rollback.tfvars -auto-approve`
- emergency detach newly created peering (if stuck): `terraform state rm module.net.aws_vpc_peering_attachment.this` then manually delete via console

ops-oncall: +1. adding these to the runbook. will watch logs during apply and trigger PD if thresholds breach.

deploy-bot: apply started. streaming: `apply: 1 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy`

deploy-bot: apply complete. route tables updated, peering shows ACTIVE.

release-manager: starting canary ramp 5% -> 15% over 15m. monitoring dashboards: baseline error-rate 0.15% p95 210ms.

10m_later_monitoring_bot: alert candidate: p95 increased to 260ms (24% up), error-rate 0.2% (ok), cpu 72%

vishal: p95 spike looks marginal but beyond our soft threshold. hold further ramping, rolling back to 5% while we dig in.

rachel: executing rollback traffic shift: `kubectl exec -n release-tooling rollout-control -- curl -X POST http://canary-api/traffic?percent=5`

ops-oncall: noting rollback and opening incident ticket. will keep oncall looped.

release-manager: adding release note entry: "Canary routing applied; small p95 regression observed during early ramp. Ramp paused and rolled back to 5% pending investigation. No IAM changes were applied."

vishal: will investigate traces and infra metrics. if we find a config-induced latency (eg route path length), we'll recreate the route in a controlled rollback and reapply.

rachel: thanks team. leaving the workspace provider pin PR open to make permanent. closing this apply thread; will reopen for follow-up once root cause identified. :lock:
